ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The function in the figure is a continuous curve on the interval [-5,5], and its intersections with the x-axis are approximately at x=-4,-2,2,4. There is a local minimum on the left side of the curve, below y=-2; there is a local minimum on the right side, approximately y=-1; near x=0 there is a local maximum, approximately y=3. Near both ends the function values are relatively high, close to y=5, so the graph can reach y=4, but it cannot be seen to reach y=-4. Reasoning: To solve f(f(x))=0, first look at the t values for which the outer function f(t)=0. From the graph, f(t)=0 if and only if t is approximately -4,-2,2,4. Therefore f(x)∈{-4,-2,2,4} is needed. Since the range of the graph does not reach y=-4, there is no need to count f(x)=-4. Thus it is only necessary to count the number of intersections of the horizontal lines y=-2, y=2, y=4 with the graph. From the graph it can be seen that y=-2 intersects the graph 2 times, y=2 intersects the graph 4 times, and y=4 intersects the graph 2 times. Therefore, in total there are 2+4+2=8 different x values satisfying f(f(x))=0.

Use the equation f(f(x))=0 by first finding the zeros of the outer f from the graph: f(t)=0 when t∈{-4,-2,2,4}. Therefore f(f(x))=0 exactly when f(x) is one of these four values. Since the graph never reaches y=-4, count only the intersections of the graph with the horizontal lines y=-2, y=2, and y=4. From the image: y=-2 intersects the graph twice, y=2 intersects it four times, and y=4 intersects it twice. Add these counts to get 2+4+2=8 distinct x-values.

method.method_draft: First describe the graph by breaking it into monotone pieces visible in the image: from x=-5 to the left local minimum the curve decreases from about 5 to below -2; then it increases to the local maximum f(0)=3; then it decreases to the right local minimum near y=-1; then it increases to about 5 at x=5.
